name: Artificial senses of touch, taste and smell
definition: Sensors that give machines a sense of touch, taste, smell or hearing comparable to or better than a person's.
what: Research on electronic noses (Persaud and Dodd, Warwick, Nature 1982) began.

sources.title: Electronic nose
sources.quote: Since 1982, research has been conducted to develop technologies, commonly referred to as electronic noses

note: Quote supports only the 1982 start of e-nose research. Earlier tactile sensors for robots/prostheses (1960s-70s) and Moncrieff's 1961 mechanical odour sensor likely earlier but unverified.

name: Industrial robot
definition: A programmable mechanical arm or machine that does factory, mining or warehouse work in place of human labourers.
what: Griffith P. Taylor built a Meccano programmable crane robot (punched-tape controlled, five axes) that stacked blocks; published in Meccano Magazine, March 1938.

sources.title: Industrial robot
sources.quote: The earliest known industrial robot conforming to the ISO definition was completed by

note: Fits the ISO definition mechanically but is a hobby model that did no factory work, so it is weak as a demonstration of factory labour. Unimate prototype (c.1958-60) and Roselund/DeVilbiss spray-painting patents (1938-42) considered; could not fetch sources for them (only Wikipedia reachable).

name: Industrial robot
definition: A programmable mechanical arm or machine that does factory, mining or warehouse work in place of human labourers.
what: First Unimate installed at GM Inland Fisher Guide plant, Ewing Township NJ, lifting hot die-cast parts.

sources.title: Unimate
sources.quote: which worked on a General Motors assembly line at the Inland Fisher Guide Plant in Ewing Township, New Jersey, in 1961

sources.title: Unimation
sources.quote: In 1960, Devol personally sold the first Unimate robot, which was shipped in 1961 to General Motors.

note: Some sources (Automate.org, not fetchable here) say a prototype was installed at GM Trenton in 1959; unverified. DeVilbiss painting robot (1940s) has no verified deployment.

name: Fully automated factory or plant
definition: A factory, mine or power plant that runs and maintains itself with few or no human workers.
what: Fanuc's robot plant near Mount Fuji runs lights-out, robots building robots, unsupervised for up to 30 days.

sources.title: Lights out (manufacturing)
sources.quote: FANUC, a Japanese robotics company, has been a lights-out factory since 2001.

note: First pass cited a 1981 report of Fanuc unattended operation (16 hours a day); I could not verify it, so a much earlier event likely exists. Date here is the latest-source date only.

name: Companion or sex robot
definition: A robot built to provide companionship, affection, romance or sex.
what: Sony introduced the first consumer AIBO robot dog (ERS-110)

sources.title: AIBO
sources.quote: The first consumer model was introduced on 11 May 1999 and was followed by updated generations.

note: Companionship fit is loose (AIBO means pal). Paro was designed from 1993 but first shown to the public in late 2001 per the page read (first pass said 1998, not confirmed). No romance or sex robot (RealDoll 1997 is a doll, not a robot; Realbotix 2018) earlier.

name: Companion or sex robot
definition: A robot built to provide companionship, affection, romance or sex.
what: AIBO ERS-110 went on sale and sold out in 20 minutes

sources.title: AIBO
sources.quote: Sales began on 1 June 1999 and sold out via the Internet in 20 minutes.

note: Paro handmade versions sold from 2004 are later.

name: Robot pet or animal
definition: A machine that imitates an animal, such as a robot dog, cat or insect.
what: Tiger Electronics released the Furby, an electronic robotic toy creature, in October 1998
note: Furby is a creature toy rather than a dog or cat, but sold as a pet-like robot. Considered: AIBO ERS-110 sales 1 June 1999 (later, higher fidelity as robot dog); Teddy Ruxpin 1985 (talking animated bear, not pet-like).

name: Robot pet or animal
definition: A machine that imitates an animal, such as a robot dog, cat or insect.
what: Furby sold 14 million units in 1999 after 1.8 million in 1998

sources.title: Furby
sources.quote: with 1.8 million sold in 1998 and 14 million in 1999

note: Toy-store scale adoption. AIBO sold only thousands in 1999.

name: Robot police and security guards
definition: Robots that patrol, guard buildings, check credentials or arrest people on behalf of authorities.
what: Knightscope shipped its first autonomous security patrol robot

sources.title: Knightscope
sources.quote: Knightscope shipped their first robot in 2015.

note: Almost certainly too late. Earlier: Denning Sentry (mid-1980s), ROBART I (c. 1982), PROWLER armed sentry (developed from 1983); I could not fetch usable dated sources for them.

name: Central computer directing many robots
definition: A single computer or master robot that coordinates and directs a whole population of robots.
what: Walgreens installed a Kiva mobile-robot fulfilment system at Mount Vernon, Illinois

sources.title: Amazon Robotics
sources.quote: Walgreens installed one at its distribution center in Mount Vernon, Illinois, in 2007

note: Too late probably: AGV fleets under central computer traffic control existed in the 1970s (Volvo Kalmar 1972-74 seen only in search summaries, central control not confirmed). Staples 2006 not confirmed.

name: Drone (unmanned aerial vehicle)
definition: An aircraft without a pilot on board that flies by remote control or by itself to scout, carry or attack.
what: DJI Phantom, an affordable ready-to-fly consumer drone, launched in 2013 and opened the consumer drone market.

sources.title: Unmanned aerial vehicle
sources.quote: The DJI Phantom was considered one of the most influential consumer drone products ever made.

note: Year of launch of the product that started mass consumer use, not a measured usage figure. First practical use (1920s-30s target drones such as Fairey Queen, Queen Bee) not dated by a fetched source.

name: Computerized economic planning and finance
definition: Computers that plan production, manage an economy or analyse and trade on financial markets.
what: Chile's Project Cybersyn linked state enterprises by telex to a central mainframe for production monitoring and economic simulation.

sources.title: Project Cybersyn
sources.quote: Project Cybersyn was a Chilean economic project developed from 1971 to 1973 during the socialist presidency of Salvador Allende

note: Date 1972 is from the first pass (October 1972 strike); fetched page gives only 1971-73. USAF Project SCOOP (linear-programming planning on SEAC, about 1951) may be earlier but I could not fetch a source. NYSE DOT (1970s) only routes orders.
